text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
Parliamentary committees announced that lower taxes, at 20, 32 and 44 percent, will be introduced in 1998.
A Marks & Spencer representative said the British retail chain would probably open its first Polish shop in Warsaw next year.
French firm Sical has become a strategic investor in Rawicz-based paper maker Zaklady Wyrobow Papierowych, with an investment of 13 million zlotys.

The treasury ministry rejected an almost certain offer by French firm EDF which aimed to be a strategic investor in the privatisation of power and heating plant Elektrocieplownia Krakow. The ministry has called for now offers.
The transport ministry's motorway council gave a positive opinion on the routing of the planned A-2 link between East and West Europe through Warsaw's Ursynow district.
The subscription price for one-year bonds due December 3 1997 will be 102.5 zlotys each, with an issue price of 103 zlotys, the finance minister said.
Police estimate that of almost 31,000 cars stolen in Poland in the first half of this year, at least 10 percent were taken across the eastern border.
By the year 2002, Fiat plans to invest $800 million in expanding Fiat Auto Poland, the Polish venture's chief Giovanni Prati said. So far Fiat has invested about $1 billion in Poland.

Bank Ochrony Srodowisa deputy president Jerzy Pietrewicz said that his environment protection bank would not need to sign any agreements on guaranteeing its share issue. According to unofficial information, the issue price will be 29 zlotys per share.
Digital mobile phone operator Era GSM, which began operating a month ago, has signed up 10,000 subscribers.
